sections.heading: 1. Sitting and standing
lines: ① Use a wedge or U-shaped cushion with a cut-out.
③ Stand every 30 minutes; take calls standing.
④ Slow breathing, soften your glutes, 1 minute.

caption:
Wincing every time you sit down? Mr Turtle's tailbone flares by the third meeting of the day.

Tailbone pain is more common than people think. It can follow a fall onto the bottom, long hours of sitting or childbirth, and sometimes it appears with no clear trigger. It can be slow to settle, but most people improve with a few practical changes.

Try a wedge or cut-out cushion, lean slightly forward so your sit bones take the weight, stand up every 30 minutes and ease tension in the muscles around it.

Pain after a significant fall, fever, numbness or bladder and bowel changes should be checked by your GP. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can assess the rest. Book online via the link in bio 🐢
